======================================================
 NIRMAL KUMAR MANDAL @ NIRMAL KUMAR S/O HARDEO  MANDAL R/O VILLAGE- BORBA, PS. PARBATTA, DIST. BHAGALPUR

... 
 Versus  THE STATE OF BIHAR  ... ...

For the Petitioner/s : Mrs.Priyanka Singh  For the Opposite Party/s : Mr.Ramchandra Sahni  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA PRAKASH  SINGH
ORAL ORDER 2 20-07-2023
Learned counsel for the petitioner is permitted to remove defect (s), as pointed out by the office, if any, within a period of four weeks on resumption of physical mode.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.P.P. for the State.
The petitioner has preferred this application for grant of regular bail in connection with Naugachhia Mahila P.S. Case No. 03 of 2023 dated 10.2.2023 registered for the offence punishable u/s 498A,
494, 448, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
As per the prosecution case, the petitioner and the co- accused persons are alleged to have tortured the daughter of the informant for demand of Rs. 4 lakh and a motorcycle as dowry.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.42921 of 2023(2) dt.20-07-2023
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
There is general and omnibus allegation against the petitioner.
The petitioner is the husband of the daughter of the informant.
The petitioner has got clean antecedent as stated in para 3 of the bail petition.
The petitioner is in custody since 14.2.2023.

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P. for the State has vehemently opposed the bail petition of the petitioner.

Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case as well as the period of custody, the petitioner above- named, is directed to be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail-bond of Rs.20,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court concerned, Naugachhia in connection with Naugachhia Mahila P.S. Case No. 03 of 2023.
